newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to auction 250 million pesos of bank assets.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to auction 250 million pesos of bank assets.

text.p: Mexico will sell 250 million pesos worth of assets seized by the government as part of emergency bank bailouts, in its first such auction, an official close to the auction said.

"The first auction, which will be convoked on April 30, will only be for 250 million pesos, and will be used as a test to see how bidders react," the official, who asked not to be identified, said on Wednesday.
He said the assets will come from up to seven large banks.

They are part of a total 307 billion pesos of bank assets that are due to be sold off by the Sale and Valuation of Assets (VVA), a unit set up to offload credits bought by the government to help bail out troubled banks in 1995 and 1996.
According to VVA director Carlos Medina Mora, that total has been sub-divided into two chunks:
-- 142 billion pesos of commercial and industrial loans that banks sold to the Bank Insurance Fund (Fobaproa) on the agreement that they would boost capitalisation levels in return;
-- 164 billion pesos of varied credits, properties and other assets that were seized by the government in its intervention of 12 stricken banks.
The official said the 307 billion pesos came from some 650,000 defaulted credits in the hands of VVA.
He said the agent bank in charge of the auction would be announced on April 29.
